events.description: House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing on Afghanistan with Generals Milley and McKenzie; blame directed at State Department for late NEO
Gen. Miller said al-Qaeda was operating 'across the country' in Afghanistan, contradicting earlier estimates of 50-100 confined to Kunar/Nuristan
Raid on al-Qaeda camp in Shorabak, Kandahar killed ~150 al-Qaeda fighters (date not stated by host)
Gen. Miller said district security status was 'immaterial' and the true metric was peace talks with the Taliban; Milley appointed CJCS (per host)
Milley said the Taliban held ~81 districts and were incapable of taking cities; LWJ counted 139 of 407 districts under Taliban control and ~200 contested
One month later Milley said the Taliban controlled over half (~220) of districts
Zaranj, capital of Nimruz, first provincial capital to fall to the Taliban
Taliban entered Kabul; NEO called only then; Afghan government collapsed ('in 11 days' per Milley)
US forces partnered with Taliban unit Badri 313, tied to the Haqqani Network, outside Hamid Karzai International Airport
Biden announced the withdrawal; Taliban final campaign began as soon as it was announced (approx)

key_claims: Congress let Milley and McKenzie off the hook; blame was redirected to the State Department and the late NEO.
US generals supported peace talks even as Gen. Miller acknowledged al-Qaeda operating across Afghanistan with Taliban support.
Milley's June 2021 claim of ~81 Taliban districts and 'incapable of taking cities' was contradicted by LWJ's count (139 controlled) and by his own figure (~220) a month later.
The Taliban's final campaign began as soon as the withdrawal was announced; Afghanistan did not fall 'in 11 days'.
Milley's ANSF (375k vs 170k) and Taliban (50k DoD vs >100k) numbers were wrong or massaged; Roggio estimated 100-200k Taliban with auxiliaries.
US forces partnered at Kabul airport with Badri 313, the Haqqani Network's elite unit.
